newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-ANWAR POWERS TO 194 FOR ONE-DAY RECORD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ANWAR POWERS TO 194 FOR ONE-DAY RECORD.

text.p: Pakistan opener Saeed Anwar smashed the highest individual score in one-day internationals on Wednesday -- 194 against India in the Independence Cup.
Anwar powered Pakistan to an imposing 327 for five from their 50 overs in the last preliminary match of the four-nation tournament.
Left-handed Anwar beat the previous record of 189 by former West Indies captain Viv Richards against England at Old Trafford in 1984.
Anwar hit 22 fours and five sixes as he made his runs off 147 balls. He plundered 26 runs in one over from leg-spinner Anil Kumble, including three sixes.
Pakistan had made a poor start, losing Anwar's opening partner Shahid Afridi when he was caught by Saurav Ganguly while trying to attack paceman Abey Kuruvilla in the second over.
Captain Rameez Raja joined Anwar to steady the innings by adding 89 for the second wicket before Raja was bowled by seamer Robin Singh for 22.
Anwar then put on 116 for the third wicket with Ijaz Ahmed (39), and Inzamam-ul-Haq gave the opener further support by hitting an unbeaten 39.
Anwar's whirlwind century ended when he was caught by Saurav Ganguly off Indian skipper Sachin Tendulkar when going for a big hit towards the end of the innings.
